sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Arduinna is a Continental Celtic goddess. Writers also spell her name Ardwinna, Arduenna, and Arduanna. Some link her to the Roman Diana or the Greek Artemis. She rode a wild boar through the Gaulish forest that bore her name, the Ardennes. Hunters entered her woods only if they left money for the animals they killed. Her name may hold ard, the word for height or highland.
objective: Record Arduinna, the Continental goddess of the boar and the Ardennes.
